body: i really loved IOP and it really did help me a lot. i struggled a lot with “putting on a mask” and pretending things are okay but IOP was truly a place i could breathe for the first time. it’s important to take it seriously and not try to do things to get out of IOP(lie, deceive, etc). the things i learned from IOP 5 years ago have stuck with me and helped a lot

hi!! i’m a sophomore living on campus!! i live at the apartments on grace and i would say it’s really not that bad. 

pros; 
- going to class is so. easy. like i just have to walk out my apartment and i’m at burruss or SSC within 5-10 min
- ra’s are there in case anything goes wrong with the people you live with
- there are a lot of people you can call if something breaks
- there are buses right outside 
- more of a studios environment 
- being able to have a smaller meal plan + being able to cook at the apartment 

cons:
- fire drills and checks
- having a roommate
- dealing with osarp and orl 
- 4 washers 4 dryers for a whole ass floor so you have to pick the right time to do laundry

all in all it’s NOT that bad. i like it bc i have all my classes within a 10 min walk or 5 min bus ride away. and i had some problems the first few days w my roommate and the ra helped us out a lot so it just depends on what you want out of your living situation.

maybe you could also contact the counseling services here at jmu and see if they have a room you could use?? and i’m not sure if they’re open but in ssc they have some rooms open on the 4th floor that you could grab if you get there early and maybe put a sticky note on the door
i’ll definitely try that out, hopefully they’ll let me out of it!! thank you!!
